name: Boneyard Pond
subtitle: Still Pond, Hive Ward
body:
A still pond tucked into the Hive's interior, far enough from main streets that only regulars know the approach. The surface is covered in floating refuse and the occasional corpse the Dustmen haven't collected yet. The smell is what you notice first.

There is no known source and no drain. It simply exists, as many things in the Hive do, without explanation or upkeep.

Someone is usually on the shore. They are not there for the view.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Known to locals; not on main streets

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A good location for a clandestine meeting or a body disposal that someone will notice too late. The regulars here are the bottom tier of the Hive's social structure. They are not dangerous but they are observant: if you do something here, someone saw it.

name: Bottle and Jug
subtitle: Tavern, Hive Ward
body:
A round tower of black granite with a tall arched door, one of the larger taverns in the Hive. The exterior is solid. The interior smells like every other bar in the ward, only louder.

The Bottle and Jug is known for nightly entertainment combat: staged fights on a raised platform, with the crowd betting on outcomes. The fighters are professionals, mostly. The outcomes are not always staged.

Nultash runs the bar. He is half-human, half-spirit: bulky, purple-tinged skin, faint wisps rising off him that most patrons stop noticing after the first drink. Brown shirt, sleeves rolled, towel over one shoulder. He speaks in short sentences and means them. The fights are called by Hidden River, a slight Tabaxi in a patchwork suit, the best assembled from what the Hive offers. He is small and he owns the room anyway.

  • Nultash — half-human/half-spirit bartender
  • Hidden River — Tabaxi fight caller

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Bottle and Jug is where you send the party when they need to find someone in the Hive. Parakk can be found by asking here. The nightly fights are real and the betting is real: a source of income and a time sink if the party gets interested.

name: Cask Family HQ
subtitle: Cask Family Back Room, Smoldering Corpse Bar, Hive Ward
body:
Through the Smoldering Corpse Bar and down a series of twisting hallways, you need to be led. Offices and storerooms line either side. One door at the end bears no distinction from any other.

The door opens into two rooms. The staging room has couches along the walls: officers and associates of the Cask Family, relaxing, smoking, waiting. A tiny desk in the corner serves as the collection point, managed by a secretary. Through a second door is Mother Cask's office. A map of Sigil hangs on the wall.

Mother Veshka Cask runs the Family from this office. The staging room is never empty.

  • Mother Veshka Cask — head of the Cask Family
  • Pell Strix — tiefling secretary, tiny nub horns, wire-rimmed glasses, never looks up from the ledger
  • Varkuun Dawncrusher — minotaur capo, Cask Family lieutenant; pulls his own oversized chair in from another room, pushing Mother Cask's desk to the corner. Open purple velvet vest, immaculate except for a broad bloodstain across the front — a betrayer's, he'll tell you if asked. May be found here when Mother Cask is absent; possible contact for Hive arc jobs.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Through Smoldering Corpse Bar, twisting hallways, unmarked door

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The back room is the Cask Family's territorial headquarters and is heavily protected. Walking in uninvited is a serious provocation. This location becomes accessible if the party reaches terms with the Family or is running a job for them.

name: Certified Fishing Circle of the Ditch
subtitle: The Only Credentialed Fishing Spot in Sigil, Hive Ward
body:
A stretch of east bank on the Ditch, just south of the bridge below the Ditch label, marked by a posted sign and a rail along the water. The certification is from the Fraternity of Order, cosigned by the Bleak Cabal. This is taken very seriously by the attendant.

Rods for rent. Bait for sale — viscera left behind by the Dustmen, though the attendant does not volunteer that information. To land anything, make a Dexterity check DC 12. On a success, roll d100 on the catch table.

Fish Fish Boot Boot is the attendant, a dabus who manages rod rental and membership cards with bureaucratic devotion. New members have their likeness captured via minor illusion for the card. Otto and Otis are always at the rail: two retired angels from Mount Celestia, in near-rags, each wearing one left boot. They have had enough. They do not elaborate.

  • Fish Fish Boot Boot — dabus attendant, membership cards, minor illusion portraits
  • Otto — retired angel, Mount Celestia, one left boot
  • Otis — retired angel, Mount Celestia, one left boot

stats.label: Certification
stats.value: Fraternity of Order, cosigned by the Bleak Cabal

stats.label: Equipment
stats.value: Rods for rent; bait for sale (Dustmen viscera)

callout2.label: MEMBERSHIP CARD
callout2.text:
Wallet-size ID card (3.375 x 2.125 in), front and back, styled like a state fishing license. Build when character art is ready.

Front: Header "Certified Fishing Circle of the Ditch" with faction seal and "Angler's License". Photo (minor illusion portrait by Fish Fish Boot Boot). License number, name, member-since date (Sigil calendar), height, eyes. Field labeled "Species" instead of sex. "Hooks Permitted: 1". "Bait: Not Provided". Endorsement checkboxes: "Dustman-Approved Viscera" and "Oceanus Day Eligible". Fine print: "Catch limit enforced by the attendant. Does not cover what the Ditch does to you."

Back: Signature line. Record-catch tally. Punch grid for each Oceanus Day attended.

Oceanus Day: Every 5 to 6 months the River Oceanus briefly feeds the Ditch and the water runs clean for about a day. Warning signs: a week out the chalkboard starts a betting pool on the date; a day or two out the Ditch smells less foul; on the day the water runs clear from dawn to dusk with Bleakers and Guvners lining the bank. Roll 1d2+4 for months, then 1d28 for the day, after each event. Keep the result secret.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text:
Certified by the Fraternity of Order, cosigned by the Bleak Cabal. The bait is Dustmen viscera — the attendant will not say so. Fish Fish Boot Boot communicates in rebuses and has developed specific fishing-related image sequences for common transactions. Otto and Otis know more about the Ditch than they let on. The 00 result is a stray portal key; you choose which portal it opens.

Catch Table (d100) — Dexterity DC 12 to land anything
d100Catch
01–05Snagged on a dead man's belt. The hook is lost and a Dustman politely asks for the belt back.
06–30Junk. Roll d100 on the Ditch Junk Table.
31–50A pale Ditch eel. Edible only to the desperate.
51–65A fat corpse-carp, worth a few coppers to the right buyer.
66–76A shoal of glow-minnows, worth a silver from an alchemist.
77–84A coin purse or trinket, 1d6 cp.
85–89A waterlogged sealed letter. DM hook.
90–93A tarnished ring worth 2d6 gp.
94–96A whiskerfish that mutters one rumor before it goes still.
97–99A record catch. The attendant chalks the name on the board and a Bleaker nods in approval.
00A stray portal key. You choose which portal it opens.

name: Fell's Tattoo Shop
subtitle: Tattoo Parlor, Redwind Road, Hive Ward
body:
A rounded building on Redwind Road, marked by a sign of a black lightning bolt in a white oval. The sign moves. The building is unremarkable except for the sign and the faint smell of something burning that is not unpleasant.

The shop offers tattoo work. The price is negotiable. The results are permanent and occasionally more than decorative.

Fell is the sole proprietor and practitioner. He is a dabus, one of the Lady of Pain's silent servants, working on his own time. He communicates in the dabus manner: rebuses of images and symbols that drift and fade above his head. He does not speak. He does not need to. At his discretion, a tattoo he applies can be rendered in a way that allows it to temporarily become a real object. This ability is not advertised, not explained, and not guaranteed. At night he is sometimes seen bricking up ooze portals in the Hive's alleys.

stats.label: Sign
stats.value: Black lightning bolt in white oval (animated)

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Source: Uncaged: Faces of Sigil (TSR 2624), pp. 36-37. The book places Fell in the Market/Guildhall Ward; the 5e map places him in the Hive Ward. Hive Ward is canon for this campaign. Fell is a neutral contact: not an enemy, not a reliable ally. He will tattoo the party if they ask and can pay. Whether and when a tattoo becomes real is entirely at his discretion and yours.

name: Five Portals Inn
subtitle: Inn and Stables, Lower Ward
body:
A crowded inn just inside the Lower Ward border, close enough to the Hive that the clientele skews toward travelers who cannot afford the Lady's Ward and do not want to sleep in the Hive. The exterior is well-worn but sound. A stable sits tucked in behind. The five elemental connections it advertises are real: water flows through the common room, fire burns in an open central hearth, the lamps run bright without oil, a cool breeze moves through the upper corridors at all hours, and the fifth amenity is unmentionable.

Rooms, meals, and stabling are all available. The rates are fair for the ward. The common room is loud most evenings.

Gurand Jor owns it. Katrina Higildra runs the bar. Neither has time for nonsense. Both are the Sigil kind of kind: they will not let a clueless stranger freeze in the street, but do not read warmth into it. They knew Horus. This was not the first time he brought in newcomers who had no idea where they were.

  • Toloin — Horus's donkey, stabled out back

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: This is where the campaign starts. The party arrived here, met Horus, and followed him to his house. Gurand and Katrina will not volunteer information but will not lie either. The fifth amenity routes waste to the Plane of Mud. It is never explained.

name: The Gatehouse
subtitle: Bleak Cabal Headquarters and Asylum, Hive Ward
body:
A tiered tower of terraces and spires rising over the Hive's rooftops. The building is large and old and well-maintained in the way of institutions that cannot afford to let things fall apart. Faces peer from the tiny windows at all hours.

The Gatehouse is Sigil's only asylum and the headquarters of the Bleak Cabal. The Cabal believe the multiverse has no meaning and that the only sane response is to tend to the suffering around you anyway. The asylum is their proof of principle: a place where the mad, the broken, and the abandoned are housed and cared for without judgment. Conditions are better than the ward would suggest. The main gate is open during daylight hours. The inner wards require an escort.

The staff are Bleak Cabal volunteers: steady, practical, and low-drama. The Cabal does not turn away visitors who come to pay respects to a patient, but it will not let anyone wander unsupervised.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Main gate open by day; inner wards by escort only

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Useful as a safe harbor and as an information source: the Cabal see more of the Hive than any other faction. A party asking for genuine help will not be turned away. Add named Cabal NPCs the party will interact with here.

name: Gatehouse Night Market
subtitle: After-Dark Market, Hive Ward
body:
The alley and yard space in the shadow of the Gatehouse sits empty during the day. After dark it fills with vendors who appear from nowhere, lay out their goods on blankets or crates, and are gone before first light. There is no fixed structure, no permanent stalls, and no sign.

The selection covers anything that cannot be sold in daylight: stolen goods, restricted materials, information by the whisper, services that do not benefit from witnesses. Prices are low. Quality is uncertain. No one asks names. No one makes change. No one asks where anything came from.

No permanent staff. Vendors rotate nightly and are not known by name.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A source for things the party cannot buy through legitimate channels: black-market components, fenced items, rumors for sale, contacts who do not want to be found. The vendors do not carry standing inventory: what is here tonight is gone tomorrow. The Harmonium does not come here at night.

name: The Gray Ledger (Shop Front)
subtitle: Money-Lending Shop, Gray Ledger Front Operation
body:
A tidy shopfront on a Hive Ward commercial corridor, odd for the ward in that the windows are clean and the sign is legible. It reads: The Gray Ledger — Loans, Accounts, Exchange. A bell on the door. A queue of ward residents waiting for service most mornings.

The shop offers money lending, currency exchange, and account services. The posted rates are real. The loans are collected. The paperwork is filed. It operates as a legitimate business in every visible respect.

Wex works the counter. He is pleasant, efficient, and knows exactly what the posted rates are and nothing else. The counting room is one floor up, behind a door that requires a key Wex does not have.

  • Wex — counter clerk, no access to the upper floor
  • Drusine — counting room, gone before the party arrives

callout.label: INVESTIGATION
callout.text: The counting room holds the evidence for Clue 3. DC 15 Perception or Investigation to notice the inconsistency in the posted ledger. DC 20 to access the back records. Drusine is gone before the party gets here.

name: Granny Nettle's
subtitle: Corner Shop, Hive Ward
body:
A cottage on a Hive Ward corner that looks like it could fall apart at any moment. A closer look shows the wood is well made, the nails well placed, and the roof well thatched. Someone has put careful work into making it look worse than it is.

The sign, where visible, reads: Wools, Silks, and Custom Imports, Inc. The goods in the window suggest a wider inventory than the sign implies.

The proprietor is not always visible from outside.

stats.label: Condition
stats.value: Deceptively sturdy; worse-looking than it is

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Granny Nettle is the Hive arc's hag shop. The player-facing card stays plain. The shop's real inventory and Nettle's role in the arc are in your DM notes only: the Arc 1 doc and the hive arc tension track. The building's solid construction is not a coincidence.

name: Grease Pit
subtitle: Food Market, Hive Ward
body:
A wide ring-shaped pit at the edge of the district, packed with food stalls on all sides and a central table area at the floor. The structure is permanent; the vendors have been here long enough to treat it as their territory.

The selection is broad by Hive standards: a wide range of foods and beverages, most of them cheap, some of them identifiable. It is the closest thing the Hive has to a public dining hall.

No fixed staff beyond the individual stall vendors, who rotate but are consistent enough to become familiar faces.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A good location for eavesdropping, low-stakes contact meetings, and picking up Hive-level street information. The vendors are locals and know the ward. A party eating here will not be notable; a party asking questions will be.

name: Horus House
subtitle: Party Base of Operations
body:
A three-story narrow rowhouse in the Hive Ward, near the ward border. It sits on a straight row east of the Mortuary. The exterior is unremarkable: modest, functional, and no worse than its neighbors.

Ground floor: kitchen, common room, a workbench. Second floor: two bedrooms. Third floor: Horus's study and a roof access hatch. Basement: trapdoor under a kitchen rug, with crates of supplies and magical items including the bag of withholding.

Horus Lanternholder owned it. The party does now. Horus kept it functional rather than comfortable. The lock on the front door is better than the neighborhood suggests.

  • Toloin — Horus's donkey, stabled at the Five Portals Inn

callout.label: NEW HAVEN PORTAL
callout.text: The house connects to New Haven via a portal in the study. Four conditions required: roof, invited host, shared meal, spoken welcome. As Horus's household, the party satisfies conditions 1–3 automatically when one member cooks from house supplies. They must still speak the welcome.

name: The Mortuary
subtitle: Dustmen Headquarters, Sigil Corpse Disposal
body:
A sprawling hall of gray-green domes and spires rising over the Hive Ward's rooftops. The building is large by any standard: wide enough to process every death in a city with no natural limit on population. The exterior is clean and maintained. The smell of preservation chemicals begins half a block away and does not leave until you are well past it.

By law, every corpse in Sigil comes here. The Mortuary receives them, processes them, and manages the paperwork that follows. Services include standard disposal, long-term preservation, records search, and notification of next of kin where applicable. The queue for disposal during high-tension periods runs several days. The Dustmen do not rush and do not apologize for the wait.

The Dustmen staff the building entirely. They are professional, unhurried, and slightly offputting in the way of people who have made peace with something most others have not. They believe the living are simply the dead who have not finished yet. This does not make them unkind; it makes them patient.

stats.label: Services
stats.value: Corpse disposal, preservation, records, next-of-kin notification

stats.label: Wait time
stats.value: Same day to several days depending on volume

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The party's first visit: three Rusted Bell bodies from the Session 1 combat at Horus House. No witnesses. The intake clerk requires cause of death, names if known, and the disposal fee. They do not ask difficult questions. They have seen worse. Add any named Dustmen NPCs the party will interact with here.

name: The Ninefold Headquarters
subtitle: Ninefold HQ and Ward Portal Site
body:
A converted warehouse in the Hive Ward's interior. The exterior gives nothing away: no sign, no marking, no decoration. It looks like every other former warehouse in this part of the ward.

The main floor is used for goods transit and labor placement. These are legitimate businesses. The protection operation runs alongside them. One of the nine corridors the Ninefold controls runs directly to a portal site in the loading dock. The portal key is a specific knot pattern tied in rope.

Salt runs meetings from a back office. His lieutenants work the floor. The portal key belongs to Salt alone.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Salt knows the portal key. His lieutenants do not. Add named Ninefold NPCs the party will interact with here.

name: Ninefold Tenement
subtitle: Ninefold Territorial Marker, Ditch East Bank, Hive Ward
body:
A collapsed tenement in a courtyard on the Ditch's east bank, at the edge of the Night Market. The building has not been repaired. The rubble has been arranged to create defensible positions. Someone always seems to be here, even when the place looks empty.

The Ninefold use the site as a territorial marker and a checkpoint: a base for ward-level operations and a watch point on who moves through this corner of the Hive at night.

Ninefold members rotate through. No named fixture yet.

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Ninefold's street presence, separate from their warehouse HQ. They watch the Night Market from here and enforce their tax on vendors. It is not a good place for a confrontation: the defensive positions are real and the Ninefold outnumber most parties in this ward.

name: Parakk Pest
subtitle: Tavern and Pest Control Service, Hive Ward
body:
A tall, terraced metal building topped with a giant rat skull. The skull is real. The building is not welcoming and is not designed to be.

Food is available. The menu is questionable and questions are offensive. Pest removal is the other service on offer: Parakk sends unwanted pests through a shifting portal to a pocket demiplane, leaving them adrift in the Deep Ethereal. He calls this kinder than what they deserve.

Parakk the Ratcatcher lives here, or nearby, depending on when you ask. He is a githzerai who has named himself after his trade. He works alone, he works at odd hours, and he does not explain himself. He can be found by asking at the Bottle and Jug, one block from the east bank of the Ditch.

  • Parakk — githzerai ratcatcher, proprietor

stats.label: Services
stats.value: Pest removal (via portal to pocket demiplane); food

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: Source: Uncaged: Faces of Sigil (TSR 2624), pp. 76-77. Parakk is introverted and quietly desperate. He works for the Us (a cranium rat collective) and is trying to free them from Ilsensine's control. He will not discuss this. He avoids combat. If cornered he uses cranium rats and his plane shift ability to escape. The portal to the pocket demiplane is a possible plot hook: things sent there do not come back.

name: Rusted Bell Hangout
subtitle: Rusted Bell Gang Basement, Bottle and Jug, Hive Ward
body:
A basement beneath the Bottle and Jug, accessible only through an unmarked alley entrance on the side of the building. The entrance is not advertised. The bar staff do not ask about it.

Low ceilings, bad light, and a permanent smell of spilled drinks. It serves its purpose: cheap, private, and attached to a bar.

This is where the Rusted Bell plans, drinks, and argues. It is not a welcoming space for outsiders.

stats.label: Access
stats.value: Alley entrance, side of Bottle and Jug

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The Rusted Bell attacked Horus in Session 1. The party disposed of three of their members. The gang does not know who was responsible yet. This basement is where they would be found if the party pursues that thread. It is not fortified but it is on the gang's home ground: they will be confident here. Add named Rusted Bell NPCs the party will interact with here.

name: Scratch Wall
subtitle: Public Message Wall, Hive Ward
body:
A stretch of wall covered in scratched messages from floor to ceiling, in a dozen languages and twice as many hands. It is old enough that no one remembers who put the first mark there.

Press a copper coin to it and it will take your words, scratching them into the stone. The message remains until it is covered by a newer one. Press a coin to a specific mark and it will read the message back.

The Scratch Wall is the Hive's public forum. Job offers, threats, meeting requests, declarations, and information for sale are all here, compressed into stone. Finding a specific message requires time, a coin, and patience.

stats.label: Cost
stats.value: 1 cp to post; 1 cp to read a specific mark

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: An in-world mechanism for delivering information to the party or seeding rumors. A party checking the wall can find anything you have planted there. Reading requires a copper and a DC 12 Investigation check to find a specific message; DC 8 to find anything relevant to a given topic.

name: Smoldering Corpse Bar
subtitle: Bar, Hive Ward
body:
A low, domed building whose chimneys never stop smoking. The exterior is dented metal and old stone. The blood-stained tables visible through the door are not a deterrent to the clientele.

The bar is open all hours. The name is literal: the centerpiece of the main room is an immolated figure suspended mid-air, perpetually burning without being consumed. Fiends, undead, and beings who would not be welcome elsewhere are welcome here. The back room belongs to the Cask Family.

Staff work the bar without comment. The bartender has seen worse than you. So has everyone else in the room.

stats.label: Notable
stats.value: Cask Family HQ in back room

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: The front bar is accessible to anyone who can pay and behave (by Hive standards). The floating burning figure is real. No one knows who it was. The back room is locked and guarded; entering uninvited is a serious provocation. Add named staff NPCs the party will interact with here.

name: The Ditch
subtitle: The Hive Ward's Central Channel
body:
A wide, slow channel of foul water that cuts through the Hive Ward. It is not a river: nothing feeds it and nothing drains it at any visible rate. It is simply there. A few low bridges cross it. The smell carries several streets in any direction.

The Ditch is not a facility. It has no function beyond existing. It does, however, serve as the ward's primary landmark: residents navigate by it, and the neighborhoods along its banks have their own character distinct from the rest of the Hive.

The banks are occupied by people who have nowhere else to go. The Certified Fishing Circle operates on the east bank. The Gatehouse Night Market sets up nearby after dark.

stats.label: Notable
stats.value: Fishing Circle (east bank), Night Market (nearby after dark)

callout.label: DM NOTE
callout.text: A useful encounter spine. At any hour there are people here who have no better place to be. By night it is darker and more dangerous. Parakk the Ratcatcher works the streets across from the Bottle and Jug, one block from the east bank.
